validated_results.title: Fish, vitamin D, and flavonoids in relation to renal cell cancer among smokers.
validated_results.reason: This prospective cohort study evaluated dietary vitamin D intake in relation to incident renal cell carcinoma among male smokers.

extraction.population: Alpha-Tocopherol Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention (ATBC) Study cohort of male smokers

sample_size.excerpt: There were 228 renal cell cancer cases diagnosed among 27,111 men with dietary information available, comprising 93% of the entire cohort of 29,133 participants.

cases.excerpt: There were 228 renal cell cancer cases diagnosed among 27,111 men with dietary information available, comprising 93% of the entire cohort of 29,133 participants.

effect_size.excerpt: There was no association between vitamin D intake (total or dietary) and renal cell cancer with adjustment for the effects of the other variables in the final model (for the highest vs. the lowest quartile of total vitamin D intake: HR = 1.0, 95% CI: 0.7, 1.4) (data not shown).

confidence_interval.excerpt: the lowest quartile of total vitamin D intake: HR = 1.0, 95% CI: 0.7, 1.4) (data not shown).

comparison.excerpt: for the highest vs. the lowest quartile of total vitamin D intake

design.excerpt: Risk was prospectively assessed in the Alpha-Tocopherol Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study (1985–2002) cohort

timing.excerpt: Person-years were counted from the date of randomization until diagnosis of renal cell cancer, death, or end of the study (April 30, 2002).
timing.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Statistical analysis, paragraph 3

continent.excerpt: Therefore, this study examines the association between intakes of fish, vitamin D, and flavonoids and renal cell cancer risk in a cohort of smokers in Finland.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: At baseline, food consumption over the previous 12 months was assessed with a validated, self-administered food frequency questionnaire, including both portion size and frequency of consumption for 203 food items and 73 mixed dishes, that was designed specifically for the ATBC Study
exposure_measurement.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Dietary intake and exposure assessment, paragraph 2

gender.excerpt: These results suggest that the flavonoid quercetin may prevent renal cell cancer among male smokers.

smoking_status.excerpt: As described elsewhere, the ATBC Study included men aged 50–69 years who smoked 5 or more cigarettes per day and were recruited from 14 study centers in southwestern Finland between 1985 and 1988
smoking_status.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Case ascertainment, paragraph 1
